brief.name: Aquatica Lumina
brief.pitch: A color-sensing aquarium accent light that perfectly matches the colors of its environment.
brief.what: An LED aquarium mood light that perfectly matches or complements the colors of your aquarium and fish by reading and analyzing its color values.
brief.who: Amateur aquarium enthusiasts (maybe on the more tech side) interested in a unique visual addition to their tank.
brief.electronics: A color sensor, a light sensor for automatically turning the lights on when the tank is dim, addressable RGB LEDs, a rechargeable slim LiPo pouch battery, USB recharging, ESP32 with hosted AP control panel for adjusting light moods, intensity, modes, timer, animations, motion sensor (mini PIR or other type) to detect fish movement which can create subtle ripple lighting animations.
brief.design: Inspired by Steampunk (in a Jules Verne under the sea way), but functionally water resistant, slim, lightweight, unobtrusive.
brief.looksLike: I'm thinking of those tasteful, stick-on under-cabinet LED lights, about a foot in length, a smartphone thickness (wider if needed to accommodate Xiao, and around 1.5 inch wide. Able to fit and adhere under the lid of an aquarium (without falling in). Rechargeable by removing lid and charging over USB C.
